contenders.handicapper_notes: Clear class standout following the scratching of early favorite Adakite. Closed with immense authority to finish third over 1450m at Kyneton despite being severely held up at two crucial stages. Brings Group 3 two-year-old race experience, enters third-up at peak physical fitness, and gets the services of premier jockey Damian Lane to stalk just off the speed (P) before attacking Mornington uphill straight.

High-upside Matt Laurie local runner (+2.5 pts home-track angle). Produced an eye-catching debut when fourth over 1450m at Kilmore after being slow away and racing greenly on the turn. By Ghaiyyath out of a Golden Horn mare, she is bred specifically to thrive over the mile second-up. Rates as the primary danger to the top selection.

Brings proven 1600m form having finished third beaten only one length at Moe after being steadied near the 400m. Has tactical flexibility to press forward (P) under Jake Noonan, though she carries 58.0kg top weight tax and must overcome the widest post-scratch barrier.

Moody and Coleman-trained three-year-old by Shamus Award who was doing her best work late over 1400m at Ballarat on debut. Inherits an ideal inside draw (barrier 3) to save ground around the tricky downhill turn, with scope for sharp second-up improvement over the longer journey.

Locally trained mare who maps to land on the fence from barrier 2. Has shown early forward speed in past campaigns but lacked finishing punch in recent runs at Echuca and Kilmore. Needs to find several lengths to trouble the principals up the steep 210m home rise.

Beaten over seven lengths at Bairnsdale over 1600m last start and carries the 58.0kg top weight tax (-2 pts). While she showed brief spark at Pakenham Synthetic two starts back, her overall profile of zero placings from seven career starts makes her hard to recommend in this premier provincial maiden.

contenders.handicapper_notes: Top selection. Strips at peak fitness 2nd-up following an exceptional resumption at Kyneton over 1100m where she was forced 3-wide without cover throughout and still fought on courageously for second as a heavily supported favourite. Boasts the highest exposed figures in the field including a 72 speed rating at Bendigo. Canonical P style stalker with tactical gate speed ideally suited to Damian Lane tracking the speed into Mornington downhill sweep.

Major threat. With the key pace influence Sabrina scratched, Cirque De Coco inherits post-scratch Lone Speed. Evaluated with Lone Speed (+6) bonus. Set the pace to finish a neck third at Geelong over 1200m (SR 75) in 2yo company before spelling. Prepared locally at Mornington by Clayton Douglas (+2.5 pts local stable edge) with two sharp trials under her belt. If Jamie Mott crosses cleanly, she could dictate uncontested around the downhill camber.

Well-bred debutante from the premier Lindsay Park operation (Ben, Will & JD Hayes) who hit at a high strike rate with first starters. Caught the eye with a sharp trial victory at Pakenham over 1000m on October 20. Lonhro broodmare sire points to speed and poise, and Luke Currie booking signals immediate readiness. Canonical P style who will look to slot into the one-one.

Local Mornington filly trained by John McArdle. Forgive her first-up run at Geelong where she endured a torrid three-wide trip without cover throughout over 1200m. Prepped with a slick local barrier trial win here on September 23. First-time blinkers applied and maps to get a far softer run from low draw under late rider alteration Lachlan Neindorf. Strong exotics inclusion.

Debuting Savabeel filly who is a full sister to Group 1 Caulfield Thousand Guineas winner Pasadena Girl. Prepared by the Moody & Coleman yard and has trialled steadily on three occasions at Pakenham. Engaging Jamie Melham is an immediate indicator of respect. May look for further in time but has pedigree class to make presence felt in a thin maiden.

Resumes from a four-month spell. Finished down the track on debut in heavy conditions at Sale in July but showed late headway. Recent Flemington jumpouts have been much improved, including a runner-up effort over 800m on October 23. Canonical S swooper who will need the race run at a genuine clip to finish into the placings on this short uphill straight.

contenders.handicapper_notes: Profiles exceptionally well mapped to Mornington 1000m layout. Draws the golden rail barrier 1 which is an immense advantage around the downhill sweeping turn into the short 210m uphill straight. Resumes off an eye-catching trial victory at Pakenham Synthetic on Oct 27 where she displayed clean tactical gate speed. Showed metropolitan-standard ability on debut when placing at Albury and Jake Noonan is an ideal tactical booking to stalk the fence. Top pick.

First-starter from the Alexander Rae stable which boasts an extraordinary 34 percent win strike rate over the last 50 runners. Prepped with two sharp Cranbourne jumpouts, most recently winning a 4f heat in a slick 46.4s on Oct 12. Benefited from scratches moving her into barrier 5 where Lachlan Neindorf can find a sweet stalking position. The most threatening debutante in the contest.

Brings the highest exposed benchmark rating into the race, having run a nose second at Sale over 1100m three starts back (SR 57). Returns fresh from a two-month let-up and a tuned-up Cranbourne trial placing behind Oak Park Mia. Her main hurdle is the barrier draw where Mornington severely penalizes wide runners over 1000m, but Jamie Melham gives her every opportunity to cross into a midfield stalking lane.

Resumes from a six-month spell with genuine forward speed. Displayed improved gate rhythm when winning a 5f Cranbourne trial in 59.1s on Oct 19. Drawn barrier 2 which allows apprentice Luke Cartwright to punch straight up to the rail and lead or sit right on the back of the leader around the downhill turn. Must lift on earlier raceday form but the gate gives her serious claims for multiples.

Local runner from the Clayton Douglas stable who gets the home-track Peninsula boost (+2.5 pts). Backs up quickly after a fair fourth over this track and trip on Oct 22 behind Deadly Force where she was held up early before working home. Carries light weight with Chelsea Thompson claiming 3kg (53.5kg effective). Solid place and exotic booster.

Well-bred 4yo mare by Shalaa out of a Myboycharlie mare making her debut for Simon Zahra. Has been prepared patiently with three trials, recently finishing second and third at Flemington over 4f. Draws low in barrier 3 with Damien Thornton in the saddle, ensuring a cozy trip on the fence throughout.
